findings.title: The in-process capture route also covers claim-verdict, which tidy already wires with its own driver
findings.action: The pass line names only the kernels that rely on the in-process route (eligible, next), so a missing tidy driver is not hidden behind graft admit's coverage in the report.
findings.disposition_rationale: The lint stays an existence check per kernel, as before; the report now distinguishes which kernels depend on the new route.

findings.title: replayDispositions memoised a partial map when a spawn failed mid-loop
findings.action: Build into a local map and assign the memo only after the loop; a failed replay now throws again on the next call. JSON.parse failures name the correlation id.
findings.disposition_rationale: Valid: a mid-loop failure would have fed later tests a truncated map.

findings.finding_id: test/graft-admit-replay.test.mjs::keyed maps assume unique correlation ids and run#seq keys
findings.title: Keyed maps assume unique correlation ids and run#seq keys
findings.action: Added a test asserting next/eligible base correlation ids are non-empty and unique and markers are unique by run and seq. The run-done marker stays excluded on purpose: the spec scopes the marker replay to the 52 next/eligible markers.
findings.disposition_rationale: Checked the corpus: no run#seq or next/eligible id repeats (only empty run-level ids do), so nothing collided today; the guard keeps a future corpus from silently collapsing records.
